question: A driver is loading a truck with several axles and wants to know why maximum axle weights are sometimes lower than the vehicle's total legal weight would otherwise allow. What does the manual say sets this limit?
choice_a: A bridge formula, which permits less maximum axle weight for axles that are closer together to prevent overloading bridges and roadways
choice_b: The manufacturer's paint color rating for the axle housing
choice_c: A rule that all axles must carry exactly equal weight regardless of spacing
choice_d: The number of tires mounted on the drive axle only
explanation: The manual states that maximum axle weights are often set by a bridge formula, which permits less maximum axle weight for axles that are closer together, to prevent overloading bridges and roadways.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-1

question: A high center of gravity caused by cargo piled up high or heavy cargo loaded on top is most dangerous in which situation?
choice_a: In curves or when the driver has to swerve to avoid a hazard
choice_b: While the vehicle is stopped at a weigh station
choice_c: On long, straight highway stretches at steady speed
choice_d: Only during backing maneuvers in a parking lot
explanation: The manual explains that a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over, and this is most dangerous in curves or if the driver has to swerve to avoid a hazard.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-1

question: To keep a load as stable as possible, how should the heaviest and lightest parts of a shipment be arranged relative to each other?
choice_a: The heaviest parts should be placed under the lightest parts
choice_b: The heaviest parts should be placed on top of the lightest parts
choice_c: The lightest parts should always ride nearest the header board regardless of the heavy items
choice_d: Weight placement makes no difference as long as tie-downs are used
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to distribute cargo so it is as low as possible, putting the heaviest parts of the cargo under the lightest parts.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-1

question: Too much weight on a truck's steering axle can cause which of the following problems?
choice_a: Hard steering, and it can damage the steering axle and tires
choice_b: Easier steering with reduced tire wear
choice_c: Improved traction on the drive wheels
explanation: The manual states that too much weight on the steering axle can cause hard steering and can damage the steering axle and tires.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-1

question: A driver notices the drive wheels spin easily and the truck struggles to keep going in bad weather. According to the manual, what loading problem does this suggest?
choice_a: Too little weight on the driving axles, causing poor traction
choice_b: Too much weight on the steering axle
choice_c: A load that has been covered improperly
choice_d: An oversized load without the required permits
explanation: The manual states that too little weight on the driving axles can cause poor traction, the drive wheels may spin easily, and during bad weather the truck may not be able to keep going.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-1

question: Besides making steering and braking more difficult, what happens to a truck's stopping distance when it is overloaded?
choice_a: Stopping distance increases, and brakes can fail when forced to work too hard
choice_b: Stopping distance decreases because the added weight presses the tires down
choice_c: Stopping distance stays the same regardless of load weight
choice_d: Stopping distance only changes on wet pavement
explanation: The manual states overloading can have bad effects on steering, braking, and speed control; stopping distance increases and brakes can fail when forced to work too hard.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-1

question: On a cargo deck, blocking that is shaped to fit snugly against a piece of freight and secured at the front, back, and/or sides serves what purpose?
choice_a: It keeps the cargo from sliding
choice_b: It protects the cargo only from rain and weather
choice_c: It replaces the need for tie-downs on enclosed vans
choice_d: It is required only for hanging meat loads
explanation: The manual states that blocking is used in the front, back, and/or sides of a piece of cargo to keep it from sliding, is shaped to fit snugly against the cargo, and is secured to the cargo deck to prevent movement.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-1

question: Bracing used to prevent cargo movement runs between which two points, as described in the manual?
choice_a: From the upper part of the cargo to the floor and/or walls of the cargo compartment
choice_b: From the front header board to the rear doors only
choice_c: From one side wall to the opposite side wall at floor level only
choice_d: From the trailer hitch to the kingpin
explanation: The manual states that bracing is also used to prevent movement of cargo and goes from the upper part of the cargo to the floor and/or walls of the cargo compartment.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-1

question: Federal regulations set a minimum standard for how strong a tie-down securement system must be relative to the cargo it secures. What is that minimum aggregate working load limit?
choice_a: At least one-half times the weight of the article or group of articles
choice_b: Exactly equal to the weight of the article or group of articles
choice_c: At least two times the weight of the article or group of articles
choice_d: At least one-quarter times the weight of the article or group of articles
explanation: The manual states federal regulations require the aggregate working load limit of any securement system used to secure an article or group of articles against movement must be at least one-half times the weight of the article or group of articles.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-1

question: A driver is hauling a 35-foot piece of flatbed freight. Based on the manual's tie-down guidance, roughly how many tie-downs should this load have at minimum, and what is the absolute floor for even a very small item?
choice_a: About one tie-down per ten feet of cargo, with at least two tie-downs no matter how small the cargo
choice_b: Exactly one tie-down regardless of the cargo's length
choice_c: One tie-down for every twenty feet of cargo, with no minimum for small items
choice_d: Four tie-downs per axle on the trailer
explanation: The manual states cargo should have at least one tie-down for each ten feet of cargo, and no matter how small the cargo, it should have at least two tie-downs.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: Why does the manual instruct drivers to make sure a front-end header board, or "headache rack," is in good condition?
choice_a: It protects the driver from cargo shifting forward in a crash or emergency stop
choice_b: It is where the vehicle's oversized-load transit permit must be displayed
choice_c: It provides the primary tie-down anchor points for the rear of the load
choice_d: It shields cargo from wind and precipitation while driving
explanation: The manual states that front-end header boards ("headache racks") protect the driver from cargo in case of a crash or emergency stop, and the front-end structure should block the forward movement of any cargo carried.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: The manual gives two basic reasons for covering an open-bed load. What are they?
choice_a: To protect people from spilled cargo and to protect the cargo from weather
choice_b: To reduce wind resistance and improve fuel economy
choice_c: To conceal the load from other drivers and deter theft
choice_d: To satisfy axle weight limits and reduce tire wear
explanation: The manual lists two basic reasons for covering cargo: to protect people from spilled cargo, and to protect the cargo from weather.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: A driver is dispatched with a sealed trailer and cannot inspect the contents. What does the manual say the driver should still verify before transporting it?
choice_a: That the load does not exceed gross weight and axle weight limits
choice_b: That the seal number matches the driver's personal logbook entry
choice_c: That the container was loaded onto a flatbed rather than a chassis
choice_d: Nothing further, since sealed loads are exempt from weight limits
explanation: The manual states that although you cannot inspect sealed loads, you should check that you don't exceed gross weight and axle weight limits.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: Dry bulk tanks are identified in the manual as cargo needing special attention. What driving behavior does the manual recommend because of their high center of gravity and shifting load?
choice_a: Be extremely cautious, driving slowly and carefully around curves and sharp turns
choice_b: Maintain highway speed through curves to keep the load settled
choice_c: Avoid all use of tie-downs since the tank itself contains the load
choice_d: Cover the tank to prevent the contents from spilling in the wind
explanation: The manual states dry bulk tanks require special care because they have a high center of gravity and the load can shift, so drivers should be extremely cautious going around curves and making sharp turns.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: Suspended beef, pork, or lamb hanging in a refrigerated truck is described as a very unstable load. Where does the manual say particular caution is needed?
choice_a: On sharp curves such as off ramps and on ramps, because of the load's high center of gravity
choice_b: Only when the refrigeration unit is turned off
choice_c: Only while backing into a loading dock
choice_d: On straight interstate highways at cruising speed
explanation: The manual states hanging meat can be a very unstable load with a high center of gravity, and particular caution is needed on sharp curves such as off ramps and on ramps, so drivers should go slowly.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: A driver is hauling livestock with less than a full trailer load. What technique does the manual recommend, and why does danger remain even after using it?
choice_a: Use false bulkheads to bunch the animals together, but rollover risk remains because livestock can still lean on curves and shift the center of gravity
choice_b: Spread the animals evenly through the trailer, which fully eliminates any risk of shifting weight
choice_c: Increase following distance only, since livestock loads behave like any other bulk cargo
choice_d: Cover the livestock with a tarp to keep the load's weight distribution stable
explanation: The manual states that with less than a full load, false bulkheads should be used to keep livestock bunched together, but even when bunched, livestock can lean on curves, shifting the center of gravity and making rollover more likely.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2
